NO. 031 · Wetlands & Waterways / Ardeidae · Herons & Egrets

Great Egret

大白鹭 · dà bái lù Ardea alba
Winter visitor Common 80–100 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

The big one among the white egrets — a yellow bill does the talking

A full size larger than Little Egret and close to a metre tall, with a bright yellow bill, black legs and an absurdly long neck. In winter the Delta's mudflats are full of them, standing in the water like white porcelain.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • BillBlack in breeding condition, bright yellow outside it — that is, right through the South China winter. Long and pointed, far heavier than a Little Egret's.
  • GapeThe gape line runs back well past the rear edge of the eye — the most reliable way to separate it from Intermediate Egret.
  • LegsLegs and feet both black; unlike Little Egret it has no yellow feet.
  • Size80–100 cm long, wingspan up to 1.5 m; neck very long, folded into a pronounced S in flight.

Behaviour

Usually alone at the edge of deeper water, standing still and then stabbing at fish, frogs and crustaceans. Its movements are very slow — it can hold a single pose for minutes. Widespread in winter on coastal mudflats, fish ponds and reservoirs, roosting communally in trees at night. Compared with Little Egret it prefers open water with fewer people.

Voice

A low, hoarse 'kraa' or 'graa', deeper and heavier than Little Egret's; often repeated several times when flushed.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Qi'ao Island tidal flats
  • Hengqin Mangzhou Wetland
  • Jinwan beaches
  • Qianwu Reservoir
Field note
How do you judge a distant white dot? By proportion — a Great Egret's neck looks out of all proportion and it stands very upright; Little Egret is smaller, more compact, and shows yellow feet.
